findings.description: Setting `suggestion` to `null` for a finding `review-spec` raised does not stop issue text from reaching a committable block. `post-review.script.ts` posts `finding.body ?? finding.description` raw. GitHub makes any ```` ```suggestion ```` fence in a review comment committable. `review-spec` is told to quote the requirement, and the orchestrator's `body` cites it. So a requirement written as a suggestion fence in an attacker's issue gets posted as a working "Commit suggestion" on the anchored line. It also skips the poster's inert-fence guard for relocated anchors, since that guard only covers the `suggestion` field.
findings.body:
**Issue text can still become a committable suggestion through `body` / `description`.**

This change makes a finding `review-spec` raised carry a `null` `suggestion`, but that only closes the `suggestion` field. The poster puts the comment text in as-is:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/30cd04954fbd4ddeeb9e6f97996b40f908b5ca75/tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts#L73-L78

Nothing in `tools/review/src` neutralises fences in `body`, and the schema treats `body` as a plain string. GitHub turns any ```` ```suggestion ```` fence in a review comment into a "Commit suggestion" button. `review-spec` must "quote the requirement it rests on" (`.claude/agents/review-spec.md` L14). It reads the issue body via `gh issue view`, and on a public repo anyone can write that body. §8 then asks the orchestrator's `body` to cite it:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/30cd04954fbd4ddeeb9e6f97996b40f908b5ca75/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L152-L154

So anyone who opens an issue the PR closes can write a "requirement" as a suggestion fence. When `review-spec` flags it as built wrong and the quote ends up in `body` (or in `description`, the fallback when `body` is `null`), the bot posts a working commit button on the anchored line. That is the path this change meant to close. It also gets past the poster's inert-fence guard for relocated anchors, because that guard only looks at `finding.suggestion`.

Fix: in §8, say that the `body` of a finding `review-spec` raised quotes issue text as inert text (an indented block or a `text` fence), never as a ```` ```suggestion ```` fence. A stronger fix that doesn't depend on prose: have the poster's comment builder defang ```` ```suggestion ```` fences inside `body`/`description`. The poster is the only place this can be enforced.

findings.description: The new `suggestion` rule has two wording problems. First, "for the reason `--fix` skips it" points at L142, which gives two reasons, and only the issue-text one applies to a suggestion. Second, "whoever would write it" doesn't say who it means (the orchestrator). Restating the issue-text clause, and naming the orchestrator, would let the bullet stand on its own. It would also match L142's "whatever area it ends up in (§6), a merge included" wording.

The `--fix` bullet stacks four asides before its colon. One of them, "a merge included", could be read as a git merge when it means a §6 consolidation merge. Splitting it would read better, e.g. "except one `review-spec` raised, even if §6 reassigned its area or merged it into another finding. List those for the user instead: …".
